experiment.domain: numerical analysis and reproducible scientific computing
experiment.hypothesis: Simpson will reach the 1e-6 threshold at the smallest n, while midpoint may appear unusually competitive on the symmetric peak if cancellation is present; an asymmetric peak should remove that advantage.
limitations: The experiment uses two analytic Gaussian peaks and one constant function, so it does not represent nonsmooth, oscillatory, singular, or high-dimensional integrands.
Fitted rates summarize the finite n window from 50 to 1000 and are not universal asymptotic theorems.
The practical threshold and grid are fixed before the calculations and do not optimize each method separately.
experiment.method: Evaluate midpoint, composite trapezoidal, and composite Simpson rules on f(x)=exp(-100(x-c)^2) over [0,1] at a fixed grid of even subinterval counts for c=0.5 and c=0.4. Compare each estimate with the analytic integral, fit log-log rates on n from 50 to 1000, inspect signed-error changes, and run f(x)=1 as an exactness control. No adaptive stopping or post hoc grid extension is allowed.

primary_outcomes.definition: Smallest declared n at which midpoint absolute error on the symmetric peak is below 1e-6.
Smallest declared n at which trapezoidal absolute error on the symmetric peak is below 1e-6.
Smallest declared n at which Simpson absolute error on the symmetric peak is below 1e-6.
Fitted log-log convergence exponent for midpoint on the symmetric peak over n=50..1000.
Fitted log-log convergence exponent for trapezoidal rule on the symmetric peak over n=50..1000.
Fitted log-log convergence exponent for Simpson on the symmetric peak over n=50..1000.
Fitted log-log convergence exponent for midpoint on the asymmetric peak over n=50..1000.
Fitted log-log convergence exponent for Simpson on the asymmetric peak over n=50..1000.
Number of sign changes in the symmetric midpoint signed error over the declared n grid.
Maximum absolute error of all three rules on the constant-function control.

experiment.research_question: For a smooth sharply localized integrand, when do composite midpoint, trapezoidal, and Simpson rules reach a practical error threshold, and can symmetry change the observed crossover beyond their nominal orders?

reviewers.focus: Rule definitions, analytic reference, convergence-rate calculation, and deterministic replay.
Look for false symmetry explanations, threshold cherry-picking, unsupported asymptotic language, and missing controls.
Distinguish observed error patterns from mechanisms and state what extra experiment would discriminate explanations.

experiment.stopping_rule: Evaluate exactly the declared n grid and both peak centers plus the constant control; do not add points based on observed errors.
